data.narrative:
ThinkOrbital is a Seed-stage space and aerospace company founded by Sebastian Asprella, Lee Rosen, and Vojtech Holub, having raised $8M to date. The broader Space & Aerospace sector comprises 6 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and ICEYE.

Of three valuation methods tested, only stage-progression analysis proved applicable. This method uses the $8M total raised as a proxy for current company value and applies a 2.5x multiplier typical for Seed-to-next-stage advancement, yielding a $20M implied valuation. Peer-median analysis could not be applied due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables within Space & Aerospace; while 14 same-sector peers exist, none of the filtered subsets (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier) contained three or more datapoints. Public-comp anchoring was inapplicable because ThinkOrbital's revenue is not on file; the sector median P/S of 27.4x across five public tickers cannot be deployed without this metric.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $17M to $23M, with a median of $20M. This range reflects limited methodological anchoring and relies entirely on stage-progression dynamics. Key uncertainties include the absence of comparable seed-stage transaction data in the frontier-space segment, undisclosed revenue, and the early-stage nature of the business, which constrains the reliability of any multiplier-based projection.
